title: One direct-image test transfers affine tensor cohomology vanishing
statement: Let S be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U an affine open, R = Gamma(U,O_S), and K an object of D(O_S) [def-pc-derived-category]. Let P be any complex of R-modules whose explicit affine sheafification F_U [lem-pc-affine-perfect-module-model] represents the restriction of K on the localized site over U. Derived localizations on S, its localized opens and Spec R are fixed, with the spectrum localization allowed an independent universe. Put j = isoSpec.inv followed by U -> S. For any O_{Spec R}-module sheaf G and integer i, if H^i(K tensor^L j_*G) vanishes in the K-flat-model sense of [def-pc-derived-tensor-cohomology-vanishes], then H^i(Q(tilde P) tensor^L G) vanishes in the same sense on Spec R. No finite Tor dimension, interval bounds, pseudo-coherence or boundedness is assumed.

source.place: Proof of (1), exact restriction and tensor; Tor testing from Tag 08CG; localized affine transport as in Tag 06Z0

proof.text: Put X = Spec Gamma(S,U), j = isoSpec.inv followed by U.ι, and R = Modules.restrictFunctor j. Unpack the given vanishing into a K-flat complex C, an isomorphism Q(C) ≅ K, and zero degree-i homology of Tot(C tensor (j_*G)[0]). Use isKFlat_restrict j to supply K-flatness of the explicit complex R(C).

Transport the existing strong monoidal structure of Modules.pullback j along restrictFunctorIsoPullback to R. The inverse tensorators are natural in both terms. In each bidegree form the tensorator isomorphism from R(C^p tensor N^q) to R(C^p) tensor R(N^q); its two naturality squares give the two differential compatibilities. Restriction preserves coproducts, so HomologicalComplex₂.mapTotalIso and total.mapIso give R(Tot(C tensor N)) ≅ Tot(R(C) tensor R(N)). This is the fully proved private helper restriction_totalTensor_iso, with no boundedness hypothesis. Restriction preserves finite limits and colimits, so the short-complex mapHomologyIso transports the original zero homology to R(Tot(C tensor N)). For N = (j_*G)[0], singleMapHomologicalComplex followed by restrictFunctorAdjCounitIso identifies R(N) with G[0]. Mapping this isomorphism through tensoring with R(C) and then homology gives the required zero tensor homology.

Let O be over-site restriction, E = Modules.overEquiv U, V = restriction along isoSpec.hom, W = restriction along isoSpec.inv, H = E.functor followed by W, A = affinePerfectSheafification, and T = tilde.functor. The overFunctorEquiv and restrictFunctorComp comparisons give O followed by H ≅ R. Unfolding A, the counit of E and the inverse identities of isoSpec give A followed by H ≅ T. First compose O.mapDerivedCategoryFactors, O.mapDerivedCategory.mapIso of Q(C) ≅ K, and hP to obtain Q(O(C)) ≅ Q(A(P)). Apply H.mapDerivedCategory with localization universes w and wX, and conjugate by its factorization isomorphisms and the two complex-composition comparisons. This gives Q(R(C)) ≅ Q(T(P)). Together with the K-flatness and zero tensor homology already established, this is the witness required by schemeDerivedTensorCohomologyVanishes. All functors and complexes are explicit; no spectrum derived equivalence is chosen.

proof_origin.place: Exact open restriction and tensor, proof of (1); explicit inverse affine transport using Mathlib overFunctorEquiv, restrictFunctorComp, singleMapHomologicalComplex, mapDerivedCategoryFactors, and the existing source pullback monoidal structure.
